[[Masami Iwasaki]] (Generations) }} |} '''Drayden''' (Japanese: '''シャガ''' ''Shaga'') is the [[Gym Leader]] of [[Opelucid City]]'s [[Gym]], known officially as the [[Opelucid Gym]], and the mayor of Opelucid City. He [[Type expert|specializes]] in {{type|Dragon}} {{OBP|Pokémon|species}} and gives the {{Badge|Legend}} to Trainers who manage to defeat him. In {{game|Black and White|s|Pokémon White}}, [[Iris]] held the title of Opelucid City Gym Leader instead. ==In the core series games== Drayden appears in {{game|Black and White|s}} where he is the mayor of Opelucid City. In {{game3|Black and White|Black|s}}, he is the [[Gym Leader]] of Opelucid City's Gym, the last Gym to be challenged by the {{player}} in the [[region]]. Trainers who defeat Drayden will receive the Legend Badge, along with {{TM|82|Dragon Tail}}. In {{game3|Black and White|White|s}}, after the player defeats the {{un|Pokémon League}}, Drayden will teach {{m|Draco Meteor}} to their {{type|Dragon}} Pokémon if they have high [[friendship]]. He can always be found in his home in Opelucid City, as [[Iris]] takes his place as Gym Leader in this game. He also reappears at [[N's Castle]] where he and many of the other [[Unova]] Gym Leaders hold off the [[Seven Sages]]. Drayden is said to train by wrestling with Pokémon. Drayden returns once again as a Gym Leader in {{B2W2}}, but as the player's seventh Gym challenge. The TM Drayden gives away remains the same. After the Gym battle, Drayden takes the player to his home in Opelucid City and tells them about the {{pkmn2|legendary}} {{type|Dragon}} Pokémon {{p|Kyurem}}. Shortly afterwards, an explosion will be heard from outside, caused by the [[Plasma Frigate]]'s ice cannon. Drayden sends out his {{p|Haxorus}} to crush the ice with {{m|Dragon Tail}}, but finds that it is unbreakable when [[Zinzolin]] shows up looking for the [[DNA Splicers]]. After rounding up all the {{tc|Team Plasma Grunt}}s and defeating Zinzolin in battle, the [[Shadow Triad]] shows up and steals the DNA Splicers, after which the player battles one of them. Even though the player wins, the Shadow Triad escapes with the Splicers. [[Cheren]] then shows up and Drayden tells the player to head to [[Humilau City]]. Afterwards, he will be in the first floor of his home in Opelucid City, where he will offer to teach {{m|Draco Meteor}} to the player's {{type|Dragon}} Pokémon if they have high [[friendship]]. He also participates in the [[Pokémon World Tournament]]. In [[Pokémon Scarlet and Violet]], Drayden is revealed to have a grandson named [[Drayton]], who is a student at [[Blueberry Academy]], a member of the {{tc|BB League Elite Four}}, and its former {{pkmn|Champion}}. It is also mentioned that Drayden is acquainted with [[Hassel]] of [[Paldea]]'s [[Elite Four]], whom he has told how his grandson has had to repeat the same year in the academy three times due to him {{color2|fff|Generation V|Generation V}} |} ==Quotes== {{main|Drayden/Quotes}} ==In animation== ===''Pokémon the Series''=== [[File:Drayden anime.png|250px|thumb|Drayden in {{aniseries|JN}}]] ===={{aniseries|BW}}==== Drayden debuted in ''[[BW033|Iris and Excadrill Against the Dragon Buster!]]'' in {{an|Iris}}'s flashback, where he was introduced as a {{t|Dragon}} Master. He witnessed {{an|Iris}} and {{TP|Iris|Excadrill}} in {{pkmn|battle}} while visiting the [[Village of Dragons]] and congratulated her on her victory. Iris then quickly challenged Drayden to a battle, which he graciously accepted. However, the Dragon Master proved to be too powerful for the young Trainer and Iris and Excadrill lost. He appears to be acquainted with the [[Elder (Village of Dragons)|village elder]]. Drayden physically debuted in ''[[BW100|A Village Homecoming!]]'', where he was introduced as the {{ci|Opelucid}} [[Gym Leader]]; and again in [[BW101|the next episode]], where he had a battle with Iris and won. Drayden was also revealed to be the President of the Opelucid Academy, a prestigious academy located in Opelucid City, where he handpicks the students to study at the academy. He appears to have an interest in Iris, and once scolded her at the academy for failing to recognize {{p|Fraxure}}'s exhaustion during a battle. It was also revealed that Drayden had talked with the Elder, recommending Iris to go on a {{pkmn|journey}}, and about the possibility of Iris one day becoming the Gym Leader of the [[Opelucid Gym]]. In [[BWS02]], [[Clair]] revealed to Iris that she met Drayden during her trip to the Village of Dragons. Drayden made a cameo appearance in the ending credits of ''[[M16|Genesect and the Legend Awakened]]''. ===={{aniseries|JN}}==== Drayden reappeared in ''[[JN065|Thrash of the Titans!]]'', meeting Ash and [[Goh]] when they arrived at the Opelucid Gym for Ash's [[World Coronation Series]] battle against Iris. When they entered the Gym, Drayden surprised Ash by revealing that Iris had become the {{pkmn|Champion}} of [[Unova]]. He then joined Goh in watching the battle. He made his first appearance in ''[[PG13|The Uprising]]'', in which he was seen outside [[N's Castle]] trying to stop the [[Seven Sages]]. Together with several other [[Unova]] [[Gym Leader]]s, he battled the many {{tc|Team Plasma Grunt}}s to prevent them from achieving [[Team Plasma]]'s goals. He then reappeared in ''[[PG14|The Frozen World]]'', in which he tried to protect [[Opelucid City]] from being attacked by [[Zinzolin]] and his army of Grunts. However, he was unsuccessful, as [[Colress]] was able to freeze the entire city using a cannon powered up by the {{pkmn2|Legendary}} {{p|Kyurem}}, while Zinzolin managed to get the [[DNA Splicers]] to further Team Plasma's nefarious plans. ====Pokémon==== This listing is of Drayden's known {{OBP|Pokémon|species}} in [[Pokémon Generations]]: {{anchor|Haxorus 2}}{{TrainerPoké |trainer=Drayden |pkmn=Haxorus |type1=Dragon |img=Drayden Haxorus PG.png |epnum=PG13 |epname=The Uprising |vajp= |vaen= |desc=Drayden's {{p|Haxorus}} first appeared in ''[[PG13|The Uprising]]'', where it was seen battling against two {{p|Whirlipede}} belonging to a group of {{tc|Team Plasma Grunt}}s. It reappeared in ''[[PG14|The Frozen World]]'', where it battled against [[Team Plasma]] once again. Haxorus's known moves are {{m|Dragon Tail}} and {{m|Dragon Pulse}}.}} ====Voice actors==== {{vatable|color={{dragon color}}|bordercolor={{dragon color light}} |ja=岩崎征実 ''[[Masami Iwasaki]]'' |en=Unknown |pt_br=Ricardo Rossatto |es_eu=Jordi Ribes}} ===GOTCHA!=== Drayden briefly appeared in [[GOTCHA!]]. ==In the manga== [[File:Iris Drayden Adventures.png|thumb|270px|Drayden in Pokémon Adventures]] ===Pokémon Adventures=== ====={{MangaArc|Black & White}}===== Drayden first appeared in ''[[PS475|The Mystery of the Missing Fossil]]'' as part of {{adv|Black}}'s imagination when he expressed his desire to defeat each of the Unova Gym Leaders. He debuted in person in ''[[PS497|Finding Truth]]''. [[Brycen]] informed him of the other Gym Leaders failing to protect the [[Dark Stone]] from the [[Shadow Triad]], leading to them getting kidnapped. Fearing that [[Team Plasma]] may obtain {{DL|Tao trio (Adventures)|Zekrom}}'s power, Drayden decided the best option was to obtain {{DL|Tao trio (Adventures)|Reshiram}}'s power via the [[Light Stone]]. As he said this, the Light Stone rolled towards Black, choosing him as the next Hero of Truth. In ''[[PS498|Decisions, Decisions]]'', Drayden and Brycen met on the [[Tubeline Bridge]] while Black trained in order to wield the Light Stone. Brycen noted relying on Reshiram would make them no better than Team Plasma. Drayden replied that they had no other option strong enough to face a [[Legendary Pokémon]] like Zekrom. Later, Drayden properly introduced himself to Black, stating he expected great things from the boy. Afterward, Drayden left to do his own business and told [[Iris]] to stay with Black for the duration of his training in hopes that she would learn from it as well. In ''[[PS504|The Cold Hard Truth]]'', Drayden held a press conference in [[Opelucid City]], where he revealed to the public that the [[Pokémon Association]] agreed to change the {{un|Pokémon League}}'s opening date would be pushed up from three months to a week. Black was horrified to learn this news, as he believed it would be impossible to win his final Gym Badge in that amount of time. In ''[[PS511|Dream a Little Dream]]'', Drayden hosted the Pokémon League's opening ceremonies. Later, Black challenged Drayden to a Gym battle, pointing out that he still had until the tournament officially began to earn his final Badge. Drayden accepted the challenge and faced Black in a small hallway. Eventually, he was defeated, earning Black the {{badge|Legend}} and a place in the League tournament. In ''[[PS520|Cold Hard Truth]]'', Team Plasma launched their attack on the Pokémon League by summoning [[N's Castle]] from the depths of the earth. The castle surrounded the League building while several {{tc|Team Plasma Grunt}}s came out and cornered everyone. Drayden and Iris worked together to protect innocent bystanders from the Grunts. After Team Plasma was defeated, Drayden and the others watched as {{adv|N}} and Zekrom flew off to parts unknown. ====={{MangaArc|Black 2 & White 2}}===== Two years later, in ''[[PS526|Mr. Perfect]]'', Drayden congratulated {{adv|Cheren}} on becoming a teacher at the [[Aspertia City]]'s [[Pokémon academy|Trainers' School]]. He revealed that he made Iris the Opelucid Gym Leader in order to focus on finding Black, who had been sealed in the Light Stone. He also revealed the existence of {{p|Kyurem}} and warned Cheren that the newly-resurfaced Team Plasma may be after it. In ''[[PS546|Giant Chasm]]'', Drayden helped free people trapped by ice created by Team Plasma's flying ship, the [[Plasma Frigate]]. He declined [[Kimi]]'s suggestion to go and face Team Plasma, declaring that as a mayor, his main focus is keeping the public safe from harm. ====Pokémon==== {{anchor|Druddigon 2}}{{TrainerPoké |trainer=Drayden |pkmn=Druddigon |type1=Dragon |img=Drayden Druddigon Adventures.png |epnum=PS499 |epname=School of Hard Knocks |desc={{p|Druddigon}} is Drayden's only known Pokémon. It was first used to battle [[Iris's Fraxure]], where it easily defeated its opponent. When Drayden was speaking to the press in front of his Gym, Druddigon roared at the crowd to get them to quiet down. During Drayden's Gym battle against Black, Druddigon went up against Black's {{p|Braviary}}, [[Brav]]. With its speed, Druddigon proved to be a powerful foe but was defeated when Brav opened a door to let in a blizzard, freezing Druddigon in place and leaving it wide open to an attack. Druddigon's known moves are {{m|Dragon Tail}}, {{m|Dragon Rage}}, and {{m|Rock Climb}}, and its Ability is {{a|Sheer Force}}.}} Drayden also has at least three other Pokémon in his arsenal as seen in the flashback in the battle against Iris. ===Pokémon Journeys=== [[File:Drayden JNM.png|thumb|170px|Drayden in {{ma|Pokémon Journeys}}]] Drayden appeared in ''[[JNM19|Thrash of the Titans!]]''. ====Pokémon==== {| width="96px" | {{ActivePoké|Drayden|Axew|Drayden Axew JNM.png|dragon|size=100px|link=no}} | |} {{-}} ==Trivia== * Drayden's Japanese Leader title is {{tt|スパルタン　メイヤー|Spartan mayor}}. * In {{2v2|Black|White}}, the only differences between Drayden and [[Iris]]'s teams are the genders of their Pokémon and their {{p|Druddigon}} and {{p|Haxorus}}'s Abilities: Drayden has an all-male team and his Druddigon has {{a|Rough Skin}} and his Haxorus has {{a|Rivalry}}, while Iris has an all-female team and her Druddigon has {{a|Sheer Force}} and her {{TP|Iris|Haxorus}} has {{a|Mold Breaker}}. * Drayden is currently the only [[Unova]] [[Gym Leader]] who is not present in [[Pokémon Masters EX]] as an [[Non-player character|NPC]] or a playable character. * As he is the seventh Gym Leader to be challenged in {{2v2|Black 2|White 2}}, Drayden is the only {{type|Dragon}} specialist [[Gym Leader]] who, in at least one case, is not the last faced by the player. **This does not apply in {{game|Black and White|s|Black}}, where he is the final Gym Leader to be challenged by the player. ==Names== {| class="roundtable" style="background:#{{dragon color}}; border:3px solid #{{dragon color dark}}" |- ! style="background:#{{dragon color light}}; color:#FFFFFF" | Language ! style="background:#{{dragon color light}}; color:#FFFFFF" | Name ! style="background:#{{dragon color light}}; color:#FFFFFF" | Origin |- | Japanese | シャガ ''Shaga'' | From 射干 ''shaga'' ({{wp|Iris japonica|fringed iris}}), matching with [[Iris]] |- | English, Latin American Spanish,
